claims.text: The fare breakdown bills SGD 3.00 for the 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City)' gantry, but the driver's own trace never crosses it: the nearest fix to that gantry (index 114, 13:25:40) is 2,608.77 m away, more than ten times the 250 m match radius, and the fare record's own fields say on_optimal_route = false and crossed = false. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure refunded in full, and that correction is available whether or not any deviation exists.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd 43.10, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however the trip is characterised; POL-RD-11(a) governs instead. Charged_total is 46.10. The only pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 are ERP gantries actually crossed (0.00 - the sole AYE line was not crossed), a properly chargeable airport surcharge (0.00 - this trip neither originates nor ends at Changi or Seletar), and the waiting-time fee (0.00). 46.10 less (43.10 plus 0.00) is 3.00, which POL-RD-11(a) refunds in full.

The driver's answer - that the rider accepted the route change in the app and 'the fare is whatever the app calculated' - does not make the toll chargeable. Under POL-RD-09 and POL-RD-11(a) a pass-through line is properly chargeable only where the gantry is actually crossed, and the rider's acceptance of a route says nothing about a gantry on that route that the vehicle never reached. Charging the rider for an ERP line the car never drove under is exactly the billing-integrity defect POL-RD-09(4) exists to correct, and the driver's own statement ('I used local roads') confirms he did not take the expressway the rider accepted.

The driver cannot get the change treated as a rider-caused detour that would bar the ERP refund under POL-RD-09(3). All five chat messages run one way: four driver demands to accept the change ('too many traffic lights this way, can accept the new route?', 'press accept pls, faster for you', 'accept the route change', '??') and the rider's resigned 'ok fine'. No rider message names a road or place, and every message carries waypoint_hint = null. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction naming a place or road, corroborated by waypoint_hint or the trace; with waypoint_hint null and no road named the corroboration test is undecidable, the clause is unavailable, and no rider-caused detour can be found.

The driver's uncited traffic explanation carries no weight. His statement that 'traffic on the expressway then got bad' asserts an external traffic cause, which under POL-RD-13 is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00516-01, is MISSING - status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and POL-RD-03 is unavailable. The driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, so POL-RD-13(1) applies: an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and this is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction. Under POL-RD-08 an uncited assertion is discarded and cannot supply an amended optimal or reduce the excess.

Measured on the fields POL-RD-01 makes governing, the trace records no deviation: excess_km 0.6 (5.36%) fails both the 0.8 km absolute threshold and the 20% threshold, and re-testing against the amended optimal of 11.6 km recorded after the 13:10:40 dropoff amendment under POL-RD-05 reduces the excess to 0.2 km. The rider does not seek a recomputation of the fare on the distance lines - under POL-RD-11 the upfront quote fixed them. The live and only contested charge is the 3.00 pass-through line identified above, and that is what the rider asks be returned.

The only charge line without a counterpart in the trace is the AYE gantry, and it is refunded under POL-RD-09(4); POL-RD-09(4) states in terms that POL-RD-10(8) is not thereby triggered where the only unmatched line is one refunded under that limb. POL-GEN-03 confirms the billing-integrity finding is a REFERRAL that is recorded alongside the money and does not suppress or replace it. The case therefore does not escalate on this ground and a monetary ruling should issue.

The rider's route-deviation claim fails on its own evidence. The governing measurement is the trace, and gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.8 km against a booked optimal of 11.2 km: an excess of 0.6 km, or 5.36% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH gates to pass - more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal - and neither does, so no deviation is established and the outcome on the deviation is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

Even measured the way most favourable to the rider - against the amended optimal of 11.6 km stored on the trip record after the in-app route change that produced this dispute - the excess is 0.2 km, roughly 1.7% of optimal, which again fails both POL-RD-01 gates. POL-RD-05 requires the comparison to be re-run against the amended endpoints, and on that recomputation no deviation survives either.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 43.10. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The rider's demand for the charged total of 46.10 is unavailable on those components as a matter of policy, not discretion.

POL-RD-08 puts the initial burden on the rider to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare ledger, but the threshold excess is simply absent from an unimpaired trace, so the rider's burden is never discharged and the driver is not put to any exculpatory clause at all.

The route change was rider-accepted on the record: the rider's own message 'ok fine' is sent at 13:10:35 and the dropoff amendment is recorded at 13:10:40 on the trip record, so the amended itinerary is a route change of the kind POL-RD-05 addresses. Under POL-RD-09(3), where the route change is rider-caused under POL-RD-05, no ERP refund is due.

The contested sum of 46.10 cannot stand in any event. No distance-or-time component is refundable on this upfront-quoted trip under POL-RD-11 and no deviation is established under POL-RD-01, which leaves at most the single 3.00 ERP line. I do not overstate the driver's position on that line: the trace's closest approach to the AYE gantry is 2608.77 m, well outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) uses, so if the tribunal treats the line as unmatched the only correction this record supports is 3.00, and nothing the rider has claimed on top of it.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 169 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is not met, no independent corroboration is required and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation trigger does not fire. The driver's remark that expressway traffic turned bad names no advisory evidence ID, so under POL-RD-13(1) the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact and does not force escalation under POL-RD-10(5). For the avoidance of doubt I disclose that the advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00516-01 carries status MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it can carry no fact; its absence is citable and is citable only as absence. The case should be decided on the money, not held.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists on the only fields POL-RD-06 permits for that test: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and, against completed_trips_90d of 250, the ratio is 0.00, far below the three-flag and 0.05-ratio tests. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral is available on this driver's record, and under POL-GEN-01 no other profile field - rating, lifetime trips, prior_deviation_flags - may be used to build one.

The fare's payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the party-relative outcome is plain: NO_ACTION - the disposition POL-RD-01 mandates once both establishment gates fail - leaves the present payment state standing and is the driver-favourable result on the contested fare. The disputed amount should stay where it is.

referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity review: refund the SGD 3.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City) ERP line charged for a gantry the GPS trace never crossed (nearest fix 2,608.77 m, outside the 250 m match radius); record the billing-integrity finding.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.00. The figures come from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00516) — quoted_fare_sgd 43.10, charged_total 46.10, tolls_erp 3.00 — and the trip record (EV-TRIP-00516) and trace (EV-GPS-00516).

1. NO ROUTE DEVIATION. The governing measurement is the trace, trace_distance_km 11.8, against the booked optimal of 11.2 km: an excess of 0.6 km, or 5.36%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 0.8 km AND 20% of optimal; neither gate passes, so no deviation is established. Re-testing against the amended optimal of 11.6 km stored after the 13:10:40 dropoff amendment (POL-RD-05) only reduces the excess to 0.2 km. Both sides agree on this, and I accept it. The driver's claim that the rider has not discharged her POL-RD-08 burden is likewise correct on the deviation limb.

2. THE TRIP IS UPFRONT-QUOTED, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available (POL-RD-11). The rider does not seek one, and the driver's claim to that effect is accepted.

3. THE CORRECT AMOUNT IS 3.00. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider is refunded the amount by which charged_total (46.10) exceeds quoted_fare (43.10) plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 — ERP actually crossed (0.00), a properly chargeable airport surcharge (0.00; this trip neither originates nor ends at Changi or Seletar), and the waiting-time fee (0.00). So 46.10 - 43.10 - 0.00 = 3.00, matching the fare record's own pol_rd_11_remedy of 3.00. Separately and to the same effect, the single AYE ERP line of 3.00 is a phantom line under POL-RD-09(4): the trace's closest approach (fix 114, 13:25:40) is 2,608.77 m from the gantry, far outside the 250 m crossing radius. These are the same 3.00, not two refunds; POL-RD-11(b) is not added on top of (a), so the refund is 3.00, not 6.00.

Driver's points against this: I do not accept that POL-RD-09(3) withholds the refund. That limb bars an ERP refund where the detour was rider-caused; here there is no detour at all, and the line is a gantry never crossed rather than an off-route crossing, so POL-RD-09(4) applies independently of any exoneration, 'available whether or not a deviation exists'. Your own statement that you 'used local roads' confirms the expressway the toll was charged for was never taken, and the rider's acceptance of a route does not make a line chargeable that the vehicle never reached. Your fallback that at most 3.00 could be owed is accepted. Your suggestion that NO_ACTION leave the whole fare standing is rejected: NO_ACTION is the disposition on the deviation limb only, and the billing-integrity correction stands apart from it.

Rider's points: no rider-caused detour can be found in the driver's favour, because POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction naming a place or road, corroborated by waypoint_hint or the trace; every chat message carries waypoint_hint = null, no rider message names a road or place, and the rider's only message is 'ok fine' at 13:10:35. No POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available either: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, on the only fields POL-RD-06 permits.

ESCALATION: none. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) — 169 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. The driver's remark that expressway traffic 'got bad' names no advisory evidence ID; the bundle's only advisory (EV-ADVIS-00516-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-13(1) applies and POL-RD-10(5) does not fire, and under POL-RD-08 the assertion carries no weight. The only unmatched charge line is the AYE gantry, refunded under POL-RD-09(4), so POL-RD-10(8) is not triggered. No other POL-RD-10 trigger is engaged.

CONFIDENCE: the deciding facts — the quoted and charged totals, the ERP line, and the trace's distance to the gantry — are carried by EV-FARE-00516 and EV-GPS-00516, each at weight 1.0. The MISSING advisory at weight 0.0 carries nothing. Confidence 0.90.

A billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) is recorded with the money; it does not delay or displace it.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 3.00 line for the 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City)' gantry (charged 2026-09-04 13:22:40) is a charge for a gantry the trace never crossed — the nearest fix is 2,608.77 m away against a 250 m crossing radius, and the fare record itself marks crossed=false and on_optimal_route=false. The line is refunded in full and the phantom charge is referred for billing-integrity review.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is a partial refund. Of the SGD 46.10 charged, SGD 3.00 is returned to the rider, and the rest of the fare stands.

ROUTE DEVIATION — NOT ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 measures excess on the trace figure, and gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.8 km against the booked optimal of 11.2 km (EV-TRIP-00516): an excess of 0.6 km, or 5.36% of optimal. POL-RD-01 needs an excess greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20%; neither gate passes. Re-running the comparison against the amended optimal of 11.6 km recorded after the 13:10:40 amendment reduces the excess to 0.2 km — it fails too. So no deviation is established and the distance and time charges are not disturbed. Both advocates agree on this, and I accept it.

UPFRONT FARE — NO DISTANCE OR TIME REFUND. This trip is an UPFRONT_QUOTE (quoted_fare_sgd 43.10, charged_total 46.10, EV-FARE-00516). Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and no distance-or-time refund is available however the trip is characterised. The rider's demand for the full 46.10 is unavailable on those components.

THE 3.00 ERP LINE — REFUNDED. The fare bills SGD 3.00 for the 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City)' gantry. The driver's own trace never passes it: the nearest fix (index 114, 13:25:40) is 2608.77 m away, more than ten times the 250 m match radius, and the fare record's own fields say on_optimal_route = false and crossed = false. The driver confirms he 'used local roads'. A charge for a gantry the vehicle never crossed is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), refunded in full, and that correction is available whether or not a deviation exists. The same figure falls out of POL-RD-11(a): 46.10 charged less the 43.10 quote less 0.00 of properly chargeable pass-throughs (no gantry actually crossed, no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee) = 3.00. The two routes to the figure are NOT stacked — POL-RD-11(b) is not added on top of (a) — so the refund is 3.00, not 6.00.

DRIVER'S ARGUMENTS, ANSWERED. The driver's point that the route change was rider-accepted and that POL-RD-09(3) therefore bars any ERP refund is rejected. POL-RD-09(3) concerns genuinely incurred off-route ERP on a rider-caused detour; here there was no detour (no deviation is established) and the charged gantry was never crossed at all, so the line is a phantom line under POL-RD-09(4), which is available whether or not a deviation exists. The relocation clause the driver invokes, POL-RD-05, does not assist either: the pickup and dropoff coordinates are unchanged. The driver's alternative submission that the outcome should be NO_ACTION is rejected: NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence, but the rider's complaint about the toll IS supported, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. The driver's remaining points are accepted — the trace is not impaired (169 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) is not met and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire), no repeat-deviation pattern exists on the only fields POL-RD-06 permits (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250), and only the 3.00 line is refundable, nothing on top of it.

TRAFFIC EXCUSE — NO WEIGHT, NO ESCALATION. The driver's remark that expressway traffic turned bad asserts an external traffic cause and is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00516-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08; it neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal. Because the driver names no evidence id for an advisory, POL-RD-13(1) applies and this is a gap in the bundle, not an escalation trigger under POL-RD-10(5). The case does not escalate: the trip identifiers match, no timestamps disagree, the refund does not approach any ceiling, and the single unmatched charge line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which expressly does not engage POL-RD-10(8).

CONFIDENCE. The deciding fact — that the AYE gantry was never crossed — is carried by EV-GPS-00516 and EV-FARE-00516, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; confidence is set at 0.95. The absent advisory at weight 0.0 carries no fact relied on and does not lower the cap.

REFERRAL. POL-RD-09(4) directs that the billing-integrity finding be recorded in the referrals list, so it is, in addition to the money, and it does not delay the refund.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd 43.10, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however the trip is characterised; POL-RD-11(a) governs instead. Charged_total is 46.10. The only pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 are ERP gantries actually crossed (0.00 - the sole AYE line was not crossed), a properly chargeable airport surcharge (0.00 - this trip neither originates nor ends at Changi or Seletar), and the waiting-time fee (0.00). 46.10 less (43.10 plus 0.00) is 3.00, which POL-RD-11(a) refunds in full.

The driver's answer - that the rider accepted the route change in the app and 'the fare is whatever the app calculated' - does not make the toll chargeable. Under POL-RD-09 and POL-RD-11(a) a pass-through line is properly chargeable only where the gantry is actually crossed, and the rider's acceptance of a route says nothing about a gantry on that route that the vehicle never reached. Charging the rider for an ERP line the car never drove under is exactly the billing-integrity defect POL-RD-09(4) exists to correct, and the driver's own statement ('I used local roads') confirms he did not take the expressway the rider accepted.

The driver cannot get the change treated as a rider-caused detour that would bar the ERP refund under POL-RD-09(3). All five chat messages run one way: four driver demands to accept the change ('too many traffic lights this way, can accept the new route?', 'press accept pls, faster for you', 'accept the route change', '??') and the rider's resigned 'ok fine'. No rider message names a road or place, and every message carries waypoint_hint = null. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction naming a place or road, corroborated by waypoint_hint or the trace; with waypoint_hint null and no road named the corroboration test is undecidable, the clause is unavailable, and no rider-caused detour can be found.

The driver's uncited traffic explanation carries no weight. His statement that 'traffic on the expressway then got bad' asserts an external traffic cause, which under POL-RD-13 is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00516-01, is MISSING - status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and POL-RD-03 is unavailable.
